newsitem.title: GERMANY: Zairean collapses at German arson trial.
newsitem.headline: Zairean collapses at German arson trial.

text.p: A Zairean refugee whose wife and five children died in a blaze at a foreigners' hostel collapsed in court on Wednesday when a witness described how he saw children trying to escape from the burning building.
Jean-Daniel Makudila fell from his chair in the courtroom as a first aid worker was telling the court he saw a dazed small girl trying to run towards the fire.
The first aid worker jumped from the witness stand and administered first aid to Makudila, who was taken to hospital. There was no immediate word on his condition.
A Lebanese man, Safwan Eid, is charged with aggravated arson and causing bodily harm. Prosecutors say Eid, who also lived in the refugee hostel, started the fire in which 10 people died in January.
If convicted, Eid could face life imprisonment. He has denied the charges.
The trial that began on September 16 was adjourned after Makudila collapsed.
His lawyer, Wolfgang Clausen, later told reporters he had suffered a heart attack, but judge Rolf Wilcken later said he had collapsed because of a circulatory disorder.
"It is best for everyone if we postpone the proceedings until Monday," Wilcken said.
The atmosphere in the packed courtroom quickly deteriorated into a noisy row as Eid's family members and refugees who lost friends or family in the fire shouted at each other in Arabic.

The fire was the worst disaster to hit a foreigners' home in Germany, and at first raised fears of a new wave of neo-Nazi racist violence similar to one which swept across the country after unification in 1990.
But police arrested Eid, a civil war refugee who lived in the hostel with his family for six years, on suspicion of trying to get revenge in a petty quarrel with another resident.
The fire killed six people from Zaire, a man from Benin, a Lebanese and a woman from Angola and her six-year-old daughter. Thirty-eight people were injured.
